question: In January 2022, which government delegated power to the District Collector to grant permission for the conversion of agricultural land for non-agricultural purposes up to ' 12 and a half standard acre against a fee of 5 per cent of the market value of the land notified under the Stamps Act'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jammu and Kashmir.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir**

 
 
• **​In January 2022, the government of Jammu and Kashmir delegated power to the District Collector to grant permission for the conversion of agricultural land for non-agricultural purposes up to ' 12 and a half standard acre against a fee of 5 per cent of the market value of the land notified under the Stamps Act'.**
 
• The **Board of Revenue** of the Government of Jammu and Kashmir published rules for converting agricultural land to non-agricultural uses.
 
• According to these regulations, **the District Collector** has the authority to approve the use of up to "12 and a half standard acres of land against a fee of 5% of the market value of the land notified under the Stamps Act."
 
• The Board of Revenue establishes regulations for the conversion of land use in the Union Territory under the **Jammu and Kashmir Agricultural Land (Conversion of Non-Agriculture Purposes) Regulations, 2022.**
 
• Therefore, agricultural land can be converted to non-agricultural use with the **approval of a District Collector** or by paying a conversion fee.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Among the various ways that agriculture has an impact on society are the provision of **food, habitat, and employment opportunities**; the provision of raw materials for food and other goods.
 
• All nations' economies are based on agriculture. **Growth in agriculture affects a nation's GDP, economy, development, and other factors.**
 
• The **largest producer of cotton, jute, rice, milk, and pulses is India.** India can now sell to every country in the world and satisfy domestic needs. India accumulated a trade surplus in agricultural and forestry products worth **$8.25 billion in 2019.**
